title: Treat chronic hepatitis D with an authorized HDV-targeted antiviral

concept.text: Suppress HDV replication and improve liver inflammation using treatment directed at HDV infection. Bulevirtide achieved European authorization, but ongoing treatment should not be represented as a finite cure. Proposed completion test: European Commission marketing authorization following EMA assessment of virological and biochemical response in HDV-RNA-positive patients with compensated liver disease. Test set by: EMA and the European Commission; the clinical programme measures HDV RNA response and ALT normalization. Reported achieved: Hepcludex (bulevirtide) received EU conditional marketing authorization on 31 July 2020, converted to standard authorization on 18 July 2023. Overlaps: INF-11, VIR-03. Sources given: [EMA Hepcludex assessment and authorization history](https://www.ema.europa.eu/de/medicines/human/EPAR/hepcludex) ; [Hepcludex product information](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/product-information/hepcludex-epar-product-information_en.pdf).

page.title: EU-authorised antiviral treatment of chronic hepatitis D
page.definition: An antiviral medicine is authorised in the European Union to suppress hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection and reduce liver inflammation in adults with compensated liver disease, meaning the damaged liver still functions. HDV requires hepatitis B virus to replicate.

goal.need: WHO estimates that 12 million people with chronic hepatitis B also have HDV. Nucleoside analogues used against hepatitis B provide no direct benefit against HDV. Pegylated interferon α, the earlier treatment option, is limited by adverse effects, contraindications and frequent relapse.

statements.body: European Association for the Study of the Liver
statements.quote: All patients with CHD should be considered for antiviral treatment

statements.body: European Medicines Agency, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use
statements.quote: There are presently no approved products for the treatment of HDV
statements.context: The assessment preceded Hepcludex's first EU marketing authorisation.

completion.title: An HDV-targeted antiviral receives EU marketing authorisation for chronic hepatitis D.
completion.criterion: The European Commission grants EU marketing authorisation for an HDV-targeted antiviral in HDV-RNA-positive adults with compensated liver disease, following EMA assessment. Conditional authorisation requires a positive benefit–risk balance, unmet medical need, likely provision of comprehensive data, and immediate-availability benefits exceeding the risk of incomplete data. Achieved: bulevirtide received conditional authorisation on 31 July 2020, converted to standard authorisation on 18 July 2023.
completion.set_by: European Commission and EMA/CHMP, through the EU conditional marketing-authorisation procedure and Hepcludex assessment.
completion.threshold_quote: the benefit-risk balance of the medicine is positive;
completion.basis: Marketing authorisation supplies the external test permitting treatment for the stated indication. Conditional authorisation establishes this capability while requiring additional evidence. The product information states that optimal treatment duration is unknown and treatment continues while clinically beneficial; authorisation therefore establishes access to suppressive treatment without establishing a finite cure.

milestones.title: An HDV antiviral shows laboratory activity and has nonclinical safety evidence supporting human exposure.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical studies demonstrate the intended pharmacological action and characterize adverse effects sufficiently for the proposed human exposure. EMA reports bulevirtide inhibition of infection in human liver cells and mice with human hepatocytes. Cellular half-maximal inhibitory concentrations across HBV genotypes and HDV isolates were 14.5–834.0 pM. EMA considered the repeat-dose toxicity studies sufficient under ICH S6(R1). These measured concentrations are results, rather than a prescribed potency cutoff.
milestones.set_by: ICH M3(R2), section 1.4, sets the general nonclinical adequacy criterion; EMA assessed bulevirtide's peptide toxicology under ICH S6(R1).
milestones.threshold_quote: should be adequate to characterise potential adverse effects that might occur under the conditions of the clinical trial to be supported.

milestones.title: Bulevirtide lowers HDV RNA at week 24 in a patient study with two-tailed p < 0.05.
milestones.criterion: In NCT02637999, the secondary HDV RNA endpoint shows a decline from baseline at week 24 meeting the published two-tailed p < 0.05 rule. The 2016 report included 24 adults in three groups. With bulevirtide 2 mg/day alone, HDV RNA declined in seven evaluable patients (p = 0.002); two became undetectable. The primary endpoint, a decline in hepatitis B surface antigen, was not met.
milestones.set_by: Myr GmbH and Centrosoyuz Clinical Hospital investigators, NCT02637999; secondary endpoint and statistical analysis published by Bogomolov and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: two-tailed p value <0.05 was considered significant.

milestones.title: Bulevirtide improves MYR202's week-24 HDV RNA response versus tenofovir at adjusted p < 0.05.
milestones.criterion: MYR202 tests superiority over tenofovir on week-24 response: undetectable serum HDV RNA or a decline of ≥2 log10 IU/mL from baseline, with multiplicity-adjusted p < 0.05. Of 120 randomised adults, 118 received treatment. Bulevirtide 2 mg/day plus tenofovir 245 mg/day yielded 15/28 responders versus 1/28 with tenofovir alone (adjusted p < 0.0001). Combined virological response and normal ALT occurred in 6/28 versus 0/28; normal ALT was ≤31 U/L for women and ≤41 U/L for men. HDV RNA rebounded after bulevirtide withdrawal.
milestones.set_by: Hepatera LLC and MYR GmbH, MYR202 protocol, NCT03546621; endpoint and statistical testing documented in the publication and EMA assessment.
milestones.threshold_quote: undetectable hepatitis D virus RNA or 2 log10 IU/mL or higher decline in hepatitis D virus RNA at week 24

milestones.title: EMA's CHMP recommends conditional EU authorisation of an HDV-targeted antiviral.
milestones.criterion: CHMP completes its review of quality, safety and efficacy, finds a favourable benefit–risk balance for the proposed HDV indication, and adopts a positive opinion recommending conditional marketing authorisation. Achieved on 28 May 2020 for Hepcludex in HDV-RNA-positive adults with compensated liver disease.
milestones.set_by: EMA, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, Hepcludex assessment report, section 4.
milestones.threshold_quote: The CHMP therefore recommends the granting of the conditional marketing authorisation

not_found: No HDV-specific numerical preclinical potency cutoff was found in searches of EMA assessments, ICH guidance and HDV antiviral-development literature.
The standalone EMA assessment of the 2023 conversion could not be opened; EMA's medicine overview documents the conversion date.

results.finding: In seven evaluable patients receiving myrcludex B alone, HDV RNA declined at week 24 (p = 0.002).
results.detail: NCT02637999 enrolled 24 patients across three groups. The myrcludex B dose was 2 mg daily; two patients became HDV RNA undetectable. The primary HBsAg endpoint was not met.
results.quote:
HDV RNA decreased at week 24 P1 log in six of seven patients
of the Myr cohort, and became undetectable in two patients dur-
ing treatment with myrcludex B alone. Mean change from base-
line was a reduction of 10 1.67 copies/ml ( p = 0.002).
